def: A unit that computes a weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias and passes the result through an activation function.
A learned number that scales one input of a neuron, setting how much and in which direction it matters.
A learned constant added to a neuron's weighted sum that shifts where it switches on.
The weighted sum plus bias of a neuron before the activation function is applied, usually written z.
An elementwise non-linear function, such as ReLU or GELU, applied to a layer's pre-activations.
A set of neurons that read the same inputs, computed together as f(XW + b).
The activation max(0, z), which passes positive values unchanged and sets negative values to zero.
A smooth activation that weights its input by the probability that a standard normal variable is smaller than it.
The flat ends of an activation such as sigmoid or tanh, where the slope is near zero and gradients cannot pass.
A ReLU neuron whose pre-activation is negative for every example, so it receives no gradient and never recovers.
The raw scores produced by a network's last layer, before softmax turns them into probabilities.
The result that a network with one hidden non-linear layer and enough units can approximate any reasonable continuous function on a bounded region.
